title: Face-Offs With China Happened in Arunachal in Past Few Days and Continue, ITBP Chief Says
excerpt: Director General Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor's confirmation — the first since July — points to fresh friction around Taksing, as the force raises drone platoons and a Galwan-style Strike course.
body:
• ITBP Director General Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor says face-offs with Chinese troops happened at several locations in Arunachal Pradesh "in the past few days" — and continue. It is the first official confirmation of ongoing Arunachal face-offs since July.
  • Recent tension has centred on the Taksing area of Upper Subansiri district; corps commanders met at the Wacha-Damai border point on September 6 to discuss the situation.
  • Kapoor says drones are the future of border warfare and underground shelters a priority; the force is raising drone platoons, running a new "Strike" course for Galwan-like combat, and building its Shaurya Commando units toward a company in every battalion.
  • The Congress party has seized on the remarks, accusing the government of silence on lost patrolling access — allegations the government has not addressed in response to this statement.

The face-off with China in Arunachal Pradesh is not a leftover of 2020 — it is happening now. Indo-Tibetan Border Police Director General Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor said on Thursday that "in the past few days, a situation arose where face-offs happened at several locations in Arunachal, and it still continues." The remarks, made to personnel in Alwar, Rajasthan, ahead of the ITBP's 65th Raising Day and reported by The Hindu, are the first official confirmation of ongoing face-offs in the eastern sector since July.

Taksing Is the Current Pressure Point

Reporting in recent months has centred on the Taksing area of Upper Subansiri district, including Asaphila near the Maja company operating base, where tensions have persisted since at least late July. Corps commanders from both sides met at the Wacha-Damai border meeting point on September 6 to discuss the situation; how much de-escalation followed is unclear. Kapoor gave no locations, causes or casualty details in his public remarks — and, as Power Corridors notes, his statement does not by itself establish that territory has been lost or patrols permanently blocked.

Drones, Shelters and a New Strike Course

Kapoor used the occasion to describe a force being rebuilt for this border. The Hindu reports him calling drones the future of warfare, warning that India cannot face China with traditional weapons alone, and naming underground shelters a priority in the new style of border warfare. The force is raising drone platoons in its border units, has introduced a "Strike" course to prepare personnel for intense combat of the kind seen at Galwan in 2020 — with the full force to complete it ahead of late 2027 — and is expanding its Shaurya Commando teams toward a full company in every battalion, alongside a specialised high-altitude battalion. The ITBP guards the 3,488-km Line of Actual Control from the Karakoram Pass to Jachep La in Arunachal.

The Political Argument

The opposition moved quickly. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh wrote that while the government offers "calibrated concessions to China," the ITBP chief had confirmed face-offs "on which there has been a deafening silence from the PM and his establishment," alleging that locals had reported patrolling points lost near Taksing and pointing to a record $112 billion trade deficit with China in 2025-26. Those claims are the opposition's, not findings of the ITBP; the government had not publicly responded to Kapoor's remarks in the reporting available. What is official is the DG's core statement: face-offs at several Arunachal locations, in the past few days, continuing — from the man whose force stands on that border.

Editor's note: an earlier version of this article misnamed the ITBP Director General and misattributed sourcing. Both have been corrected.
nri_angle: A verified status report on the India-China border for diaspora readers: fresh face-offs confirmed in Arunachal's Taksing sector, a corps-commander channel already used once, and a political fight in Delhi over what it means.
